newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vienna police arrest two for Man Utd shooting.
newsitem.headline: Vienna police arrest two for Man Utd shooting.

text.p: Austrian police on Sunday arrested two Austrian men suspected of shooting at a group of Manchester United soccer fans, wounding two, after a row in a bar in a red light district of Vienna.
"We arrested two Austrian men on Sunday afternoon," police spokesman Walter Czapek told Reuters. "It seems they are the men we have been searching for since early Friday morning."
One of the men had confessed to shooting at the Britons, saying he only wanted to frighten them, the spokesman added.

Gunmen opened fire from a white Mercedes saloon which sped past the four Manchester United fans in the early hours of Friday as they made their way back to their hotel from the Piccolo Sauna bar near Vienna's Ernst Happel football stadium.
Steven Mark Day, 33, who was hit in the stomach, underwent a three-hour abdominal operation. Christopher Mackenner was shot in the right leg. Both are recovering in hospital.
Czapek said police encountered no resistance when they arrested the two Austrians, named only as Alfred G., 34, and Willibald K., 44.
Alfred G. confessed he had been drunk and shot at the fans, who had come for a European Champions' league match on Wednesday night against Rapid Vienna. Manchester United won 2-0.
"He said he did not want to hurt the fans, just frighten them a bit," Czapek said.
Willibald K. had allegedly driven the car but had fired no shots, Czapek added.
The row did not appear to have any connection with the match, girls or politics, he noted.
"It was a completely stupid row," he said, but he gave no further details of the argument.
The two uninjured fans were believed to have returned to England, Czapek said.
